title: Handshake lifecycle — dollar & latency tracebook (draft)
content:
Purpose
Quick labbook for different client-server handshake strategies and their amortized latency vs dollar impact. This is a working artifact for console + SDK teams to decide whether to promote a "fast-connect" API surface vs continuing to invest in long-lived session affinity. Not an exhaustive perf paper — snapshot of experiments, numbers, and open questions.

Executive summary (short)
- Warm pooled handshakes (session reuse, keepalive, lightweight resumption) reduce end-to-end p50 by ~30–45ms vs fresh full-handshake on our sample models and reduce amortized dollar per interactive query by ~8–12% under typical short-turn chat workloads.
- Fastpath handshake (best-effort short TCP/TLS optimizations + early request multiplex) reduces p50 significantly for single-shot flows but increases p99 tail variability unless paired with admission control.
- Cold full-handshake (fresh connection + model load on warm but never-initialized worker) is expensive in both latency and dollars for intermittent workloads; optimize via pre-warming heuristics or lightweight resumption tokens.

Scope and constraints
- Models: bert-sim-small (proxy for 7B open model), llama-mini-proto (quantized), and a 13B LLM-ish microbenchmark.
- Hardware: vCPU-heavy client simulation, inference backends on g4-like GPU pool.
- Traffic shapes: 80–20 short-turn chat (avg prompt+reply length ~120 tokens), single-shot prompts (median 8 tokens), and sporadic ephemeral calls (infrequent, 1/min per client).
- Cost model: unit GPU-minute + amortized cold-start energy cost + request-level egress. Converted to $ per 1k requests using current internal price model.
- Measurements: 5 runs, 95% bootstrap CI reported where relevant.

Bench modes defined (short names used below)
- FRESH: new TCP/TLS handshake + cold scheduler placement (no prior slot) -> worst-case cold path.
- RESUME: lightweight session resumption tokens (keep KV cache affinity) -> medium.
- POOLED: long-lived connection + pinned session on same worker where KV cached -> best-case for latency.
- FASTPATH: optimistic early-request multiplexing before TLS completion (lab feature) -> speculative low p50, unstable p99.

Key numeric summary (chaty workload, 1000 concurrent sessions, avg 120 tokens)
- Model: llama-mini-proto | Mode: POOLED | p50 end2end: 180ms | p90: 420ms | p99: 920ms | $/1k: $11.2
- Model: llama-mini-proto | Mode: RESUME | p50: 215ms | p90: 500ms | p99: 1.0s | $/1k: $12.0
- Model: llama-mini-proto | Mode: FRESH | p50: 260ms | p90: 680ms | p99: 1.6s | $/1k: $14.1
- Model: llama-mini-proto | Mode: FASTPATH | p50: 150ms | p90: 560ms | p99: 2.4s | $/1k: $12.8
Notes: p50 improvements capture handshake latency + kvcache warm; FASTPATH pushes p50 down but greatly widens p99. Cost differences largely driven by worker slot occupancy (POOLED reduces redundant cold-work).

ASCII charts (p50 vs $/1k) — small spark-grid by mode (scale bar: p50 in ms, $/1k in USD)
POOLED   |■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 180ms | $$$$ (11.2)
RESUME   |■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 215ms | $$$$$ (12.0)
FRESH    |■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 260ms | $$$$$$ (14.1)
FASTPATH |■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 150ms | $$$$$ (12.8)
Legend: each block ~15ms; $ symbols approximate $/1k buckets

Tail shape observations (p99 behavior)
- POOLED: tail dominated by scheduler jitter and encode/decode serialization stalls — relatively stable.
- RESUME: occasional asset rehydration (slower KV read) causes spikes ~300–600ms extra.
- FRESH: combination of worker boot (if we evicted) and full TLS handshake drives long tails (1–3s observed).
- FASTPATH: when fastpath admission fails (5–12% attempts), fallback to FRESH occurs, creating a fat right tail.

Micro breakdown (typical POOLED request, numbers in ms)
- Client TTFB (network): 20ms
- TLS/handshake overhead (amortized): 2ms (keepalive)
- Request queueing: 12ms
- Decode (model): 110ms
- Postprocessing/serialize: 36ms
Total: 180ms (matches measurement)
FRESH extra components:
- TLS full: +28–48ms
- Worker init/placement micro-cost: +40–220ms (depends on cold)

Cost amortization note
- The $/1k figure assumes session locality: POOLED means multiple requests per worker slot over 1–3 minute horizon; FRESH assumes many slots are only used for single request which inflates $/1k by ~25–40% in this sample.

Developer impact & product tradeoffs
- SDK: encourage connection pooling, auto-resume tokens, and provide simple L2 primitives to opt into FASTPATH. Default should be RESUME for new SDK to balance cost/safety.
- Console: surface per-api-route handshake miss rate, connection churn, and per-route amortized $/1k so product can flag expensive routes.
- Platform: consider soft-eviction windows (extend slot lifetime by small delta for high-prob churn clients) — saves cost at minimal resource footprint.

Open questions / next experiments
- How do these numbers change for very low-latency edge regions (regional proxies) vs central core? Run same bench with edge proxied paths.
- Can we detect failing FASTPATH attempts earlier and route to RESUME to reduce p99? Build a micro-probe.
- Measure memory/KV rehydration time distribution in RESUME path with different persistence backends (redis vs local on-disk).
- Instrument handshake failure taxonomy in traces (TLS fail, admission fail, scheduler preempt).

Actionable TODOs (short)
- [ ] Instrument per-route handshake fallback counters in telemetry (Evan)
- [ ] Prototype SDK auto-resume token flow + opt-in FASTPATH flag (Liu)
- [ ] Run an edge vs core bench (Marta) and report delta by 2026-04-01
- [ ] Add amortized cost field to console route view (Aisha + Product)

Raw experiment notes (for reproducibility)
- Harness: local-go harness that spins 1200 concurrent goroutines, each simulating a client session with adjustable session lifetimes.
- Duration: 20 minute steady-state window after 5 minute warmup.
- Data collected: per-request timestamps for connection start, TLS complete, request enqueue, response first-byte, model decode start/finish, response end. Also recorded slot allocation events, eviction logs, and CPU/GPU flame counters.
- Config snippets: default keepalive 90s; datasource: redis-kv with 50ms median read in RESUME path (tunable).

Notes to reviewer
This is a bench-sketch intended for engineering teams to reason about defaults in SDK and console productization. Numbers are for relative comparison; do not cite externally without re-running against latest infra. Feedback: prioritize adding the per-route amortized $/1k column to console and get consensus on default SDK mode (current recommendation: RESUME).

Appendix: short glossary
- Handshake: connection establishment (TCP/TLS) + any token exchange we perform before request.
- KV cache rehydration: restoring model conversation state to worker memory from shared store.
- Fastpath: speculative early-request multiplex before full handshake/placement finishes.

---
End of draft tracebook entry.
